pion_cyclotomic_heegner.substrate: Sum of two Hubble values (Phi_12=H_0_SH0ES + Heegner_67=H_0_Planck) as substrate integers equals the charged pion mass in MeV.  The cyclotomic-Heegner identity Phi_12 + Heegner_67 = 2 Phi_4 Phi_6 is exact at q=3.

prime_index_heegner_19.interpretation: The 19th prime IS the 8th Heegner discriminant.  Together with p_(q*Phi_6) = Phi_12 and p_(q*p_Ih) = alpha^-1 = 137, this is the third substrate-clean prime-index identity tying substrate primitives to prime values.

heegner_physics_map.physics: m_s/m_u quark mass ratio; central f-lattice point
H_0_Planck (km/s/Mpc); m_p factor; alpha^-1 building block; m_tau formula
m_t = Heegner_163 + Phi_4 (top quark mass in GeV)

headline:
TWO NEW SUBSTRATE IDENTITIES:

(1) Pion-cyclotomic-Heegner:
    Phi_12 + Heegner_67 = 2 * Phi_4 * Phi_6
    73 + 67 = 140 = 2 * 10 * 7 = m_pi+ (MeV; PDG 139.57, 0.31%)

(2) Prime-index of Heegner:
    p_{Heegner_19} = Heegner_67
    p_19 = 67  (the 19th prime IS the 8th Heegner discriminant)

Substrate prime-index family (all three):
    p_{q*Phi_6}   = Phi_12      = 73   (H_0_SH0ES)
    p_{Heegner_19} = Heegner_67  = 67   (H_0_Planck)
    p_{q*p_Ih}    = 137         (alpha^-1)

Heegner pair sums:
    Heegner_67 + Heegner_19 = 2 * Heegner_43 = 86
    Heegner_43 + Heegner_163 = (mu+1)*v+q! = 206 = m_mu/m_e ratio
    Phi_12 + Heegner_67 = 2*Phi_4*Phi_6 = m_pi+ (MeV)

Heegner physics map: each large Heegner controls a distinct sector
    19  -> f-lattice anchor (smallest Heegner)
    43  -> m_s/m_u (light quark ratio)
    67  -> H_0_Planck + alpha^-1 + m_p factor
    163 -> m_t = Heegner_163 + Phi_4 (top quark mass)
